Svidrigaïlov, Bending Down with Elbows on the Window Sill, Gazed for Five Minutes
into the Darkness. The boom of a cannon, followed by a second one, resounded in the darkness
of the night. Ah, the signal! The river is overflowing! he thought. By morning it will
be swirling down the street in the lower parts, flooding the basements and cellars. The cellar
rats will swim out, and men will curse in the rain and wind as they drag their rubbish
to their upper stories. What time is it now? And he had hardly thought it when, somewhere
near, a clock on the wall, ticking away hurriedly, struck three.
